lines.text: Tighten up!
Hold still, this might sting.
Catch!
Spanner in the works!
Nice and tidy.
Ow. Just... ow.
Zap!
Sprocket storm!
Rust never sleeps!
Now we're cooking!
I knew that would work.
That was... unplanned.
Have a nice cuppa.
Mind your manners!
Scones all round!
Snug as a bug!
And stay out of my kitchen.
Oh, my poor oven...
GEAR SLAM!
Hot enough for you?
Cogs! To me!
NOW I'M CROSS!
Right. New town, new start. I will keep my head down and not fix anything that is not broken.
Gears do not just walk off by themselves.
Thank you, Trina. It is lovely. Slightly warm, though.
Are you sure? There are a lot of crabs.
A trail of oil? Where does it lead?
Leave it with me, Mayor. I will bring it home.
Bertha only wanted something that ticked like a heart. Perhaps she could visit the lane for tea.
Scrap everywhere. Trina would be thrilled. Everything out here is a bit too keen to be friends, though.
A kettle in all this? Mabel did say a crab dragged it. At least the crab has taste.
Neither, thank you. I only just unpacked.
That is Mabel's kettle. Sorry, crab. It is a good kettle, but it is not yours.
Wick, from Coppergate Lane. Hello, Bertha. I think you have the Mayor's Golden Gear.
Why take it, Bertha? You could have just asked.
There you are! I knew it was you. That squeaky floorboard gives everyone away. Wick, we have a crisis.
Mayor Pilcrow's Golden Gear has gone missing, right out of its case in the Hall. He has been wailing since breakfast, and it is very bad for business.
My point exactly! Go and hear him out. The Hall is the big building to the south-west. And I could use five bits of scrap metal, too.
Something marvellous. It has gears, a kettle, and possibly a small cannon. Do not tell Mabel about the cannon.
Splendid. Scrap is easy to find: the critters out in the Whistling Wilds are practically made of it. Cog Sprites, Rust Crabs, you name it.
And mind yourself out there. A wrench is a fine thing, but nobody ever regretted a second pair of hands.
Have you seen the Mayor yet? The Hall is south-west of here. Mind the steps, they are wobbly.
Bertha? Big Bertha?! Oh, that is bad. That is very bad. She is a clanking brute who lives at the end of Gutter Gully, past the Whistling Wilds.
Level up a little first. And bring scrap, always bring scrap. Come to think of it, I should come along. Somebody has to keep an eye on you.
Five scraps and I am yours. Well. Yours for a week or so. I do get bored.
Five scraps, just like that! You marvel. Here, I finished it: a Spark Rod. Zap responsibly.
That is the cannon. I mean, the coil. Anyway! I am coming with you. Someone has to keep you from tightening things that should stay loose.
You got it back from Bertha? Take it to the Mayor right now, before it hums itself to bits.
The lane has never been so quiet. I may build a louder clock.
Oh, I like her. Ow! Do not hit me yet, I have not finished my sentence!
And I will teach you to build your own humming thing. Gently. With fewer fists.
Oh, thank goodness, a friendly face. A nasty Rust Crab dragged my copper kettle off to Gutter Gully, and without it I cannot brew a thing.
No brewing, no scones. It is a catastrophe of pastry. The Gully is south of the Whistling Wilds. Bring my kettle home, dear, and the ovens are yours.
Big enough to carry a kettle, and cross enough to keep it. Bring a friend. Or a cosh.
Bless you. And do keep some tea in your pockets. Chamomile, for the nerves. Bertram sells it, the old skinflint.
Mind the crabs down in the Gully, dear. They pinch.
My kettle! Oh, you wonderful thing! A dent, and a bit of rust. Nothing a good scrub will not mend. Here, scones, on the house.
Now. I have been stuck in that bakery for forty years, and I have just discovered I miss an adventure. I am coming with you.
Dear, I have a rolling pin and no patience left. Let them come.
Fresh scones today, love. You have earned first pick.
Now, now, dear. Put the gear down. Nobody needs to get cross.
Oh, you poor lamb. Come down to the lane when you can. I will put the kettle on.
Ah. A new face. You must be the one the whole lane has been whispering about. Forgive the state of me. I am quite undone.
The Golden Gear has been in my family six generations. It sat in that glass case every day of my life. Last night: gone. One loose floorboard and a trail of oil.
South, through the Whistling Wilds and down into Gutter Gully. There is only one creature that clanks enough to leave a trail like that: Big Bertha.
She lairs behind an iron door at the end of the Gully. Take this brass pass, it opens the door, and do be careful. She hits a good deal harder than she looks.
Splendid. Win a few fights on the way, there is no shame in it. Bertha is stronger than anything in the Wilds.
Bertha lairs behind the iron door at the end of Gutter Gully, my friend. A few victories under your belt first would be wise.
My Golden Gear! You magnificent soul. It hums. It has not hummed in six generations.
Tea? With Big Bertha? Hm. Hm! Why ever not. Coppergate always had room for one more odd neighbour.
The lane sleeps easy, thanks to you.
Hm. Customer. Do not touch the clock, it is broken. Do not touch the cat, it is worse.
What can I do for you?
Mind the tea. It is better than it looks.
Second door on the left. Do not wind the cuckoo.
The shop clock stopped last week. It needs three Coiled Springs, and the wolves in the Gully carry them. If you bring me some, I will make it worth your while.
Hm. Good. Do not dawdle.
Three springs. Not a hair out of place. Here, take this: a lucky charm my grandmother swore by. Nobody has ever proved her wrong.
The clock is ticking again. That is the loudest thing in my life, and I am delighted.
Hm. Door is that way.
WHO IS THAT, STOMPING IN MY LAIR?
MINE! It hums at night! Nobody else hums at night! I will not give it back!
TOO LATE. I AM ALREADY CROSS. COME AND TAKE IT, TINY WRENCH-PERSON!
Ow. Ow, ow, ow. Fine! Fine. Take it. It was getting a bit loud anyway.
Nobody ever talks to me. Everybody runs. It hummed, and I was lonely. That is all.
Really? Tea? Humming things? Oh. Oh, that is... all right, then.
